counting.sequence.recite.root_reason: The number words one through nineteen are memorized as a rote sequence; a child needs no earlier skill in this map to say them in order.

edges.why: Counting backward reverses the memorized forward order of number words, so the learner must already hold that order to run it in reverse.

counting.one-to-one.root_reason: The assessment credits tagging each object exactly once with any number words, whether or not they are in conventional order, so neither the word sequence nor any quantity idea is required.

cardinality.small-number-words.root_reason: This is the first mapping of the words one, two and three to exact quantities, learned from experience with small sets before counting is used to find how many.

edges.why: A collection counted correctly requires the number words said in their conventional order, and the last of those words is what names the total.

The statement refers to the word after n in the count sequence, so the learner must know which word follows each given word.

Telling how many claps there were means reporting the last word said as the total, even though the claps are no longer present.
Reading a numeral means saying the number word it stands for, so the learner must already know the spoken number words from one to nine.

subitizing.nonverbal.root_reason: Making a matching set after a glimpse uses direct perception of small exact quantity and requires no number words, so nothing earlier in the map is needed.

edges.why: Each part of the arrangement, such as the five and the two, must itself be named at a glance, which is the perceptual skill.
Knowing the whole the recognized parts make means finding the total of two sets joined together, the meaning of joining and counting all.

comparing.count.perceptual.root_reason: Telling which of two very unequal sets has more uses direct perception of large quantity differences, with no counting or other earlier skill in this map.

edges.why: Judging that three cars and three buttons are the same number requires apprehending each small set's exact quantity directly without words, even when the objects differ.

comparing.count.matching.root_reason: Pairing each object in one collection with an object in the other uses no number words or counting, so a child can do it with nothing earlier in the map.

edges.why: Steps one and two count each collection to get its number, and the test problem counts six buttons and four blocks.
